To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the complete loss of function (cLoF) of SMS results in a severe and often fatal form of Snyder-Robbins syndrome.
the complete loss of function in the spermine-synthase gene (SMS) results in a severe and early fatal form of Snyder-Robsinson syndrome.
a complete loss of function variant in the SMS gene causes a severe form of SRS.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the first description of the complete loss of functional SMS protein in a male patient.
the identification and characterization of the first complete loss of function variant in the SMS gene in a patient with Snyder-Robinson Syndrome.
the identification of novel pathogenic variants in genes associated with X-linked intellectual disability (XLID) and/or X-linked syndromes (XLSS).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
complete loss of function results in the most severe form of SRS.
variants causing complete loss of function in the SMS protein lead to a more severe form of the syndrome, while variants causing a partial loss of function lead to a milder form of the syndrome.
complete LoF of the SMS gene leads to a more severe form of Snyder Robinson syndrome, while partial LoF of this gene is associated with a milder form of this syndrome.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
complete LoF variants in SMS are more severe than missense LoF variants.
a complete loss of function in the spermine synthesis pathway leads to a severe form of SRS, whereas a partial loss of function results in a milder form.
complete LoF variants of SMS are likely to result in a more severe form of Snyder Robinson Syndrome.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the severity of the disease is not related to the age at which the patient was diagnosed, as has been reported previously.
complete loss of function variants in SMS are associated with a severe form and early death of Snyder-Robison syndrome.
complete LoF variants in SMS are associated with a severe phenotype and are likely to be associated with early death.
